item.text:
**Supported Fact**

Under the current official MCP spec, a modern stdio server does **not** have an `initialize` phase at all: the spec says there is “no negotiation handshake,” that modern versions are `2026-07-28` and later, and that legacy versions are the ones with an `initialize` handshake. Source: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/versioning

The current revision also states, in its changelog, that MCP was made stateless and that the `initialize` / `notifications/initialized` handshake was removed. Source: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/changelog

For version negotiation in the current revision, every request carries the protocol version in `params._meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion"]`; on stdio there is no header layer, so that metadata stays inside the JSON-RPC body. If the server does not support the requested version, it must return `UnsupportedProtocolVersionError` listing the versions it does support. Sources: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/versioning https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports/stdio https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/schema

A current stdio server must speak JSON-RPC 2.0 over newline-delimited framing: it reads JSON-RPC messages from `stdin`, writes JSON-RPC messages to `stdout`, sends one JSON-RPC message per line, must not put embedded newlines inside a message, and must not write anything non-MCP to `stdout`. It may write UTF-8 logs to `stderr`. Sources: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports/stdio https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic

A current server must implement `server/discover`. On stdio, a dual-era client that supports both modern and legacy MCP should probe with `server/discover` first; if it gets a modern result or a recognized modern error such as `UnsupportedProtocolVersionError`, it should stay on modern semantics and not fall back to `initialize`. Sources: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/discover https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/versioning https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports/stdio

For `tools/list`, the current spec says that any server that supports tools must declare the `tools` capability. A server that declares that capability must answer `tools/list` with the tools currently available to the requesting client. The set may be empty and may change over time, but it must not vary per connection or as a side effect of other requests on that connection. It may vary by authorization presented on the request, and the server should return tools in a deterministic order. Source: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/tools

`tools/list` is a client-to-server JSON-RPC request whose method is `tools/list`; it supports pagination via an optional cursor in `params`, and the successful result includes a `tools` array. Sources: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/tools https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/schema

In the current schema, a successful `tools/list` result must include `resultType`, `ttlMs`, `cacheScope`, and `tools`; `nextCursor` is optional. `resultType` is required for servers implementing this protocol version. Source: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/schema

Every current `tools/list` request must include the required `_meta` request fields, including `io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion` and `io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities`; `io.modelcontextprotocol/clientInfo` is recommended but not required. Sources: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/tools https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/schema

**Legacy-Only Fact**

If a server is intentionally supporting a legacy MCP revision instead of modern MCP, then `initialize` is required there: in the `2025-11-25` spec, initialization had to be the first interaction, the client had to send `initialize` with protocol version, client capabilities, and client info, and the server had to respond with its own protocol version, capabilities, and server info. After that, the client had to send `notifications/initialized`. Source: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/lifecycle

In that legacy revision, version negotiation happened inside `initialize`: if the server supported the client’s requested version, it had to echo it back; otherwise it had to reply with another version it supported, and the client should disconnect if it did not support that returned version. Source: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/lifecycle

The **current** spec treats that legacy behavior as backward compatibility only: a server may implement both modern and legacy behavior, and an `initialize` request selects legacy semantics. A modern-only server is not required to support `initialize`; it should, however, include supported protocol versions in any error it returns to an `initialize` request so legacy clients get a useful diagnostic. Source: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/versioning

**Disagreement Inside The Official Docs**

I found one internal inconsistency on the official site: the current spec overview says extensions are “negotiated during initialization,” but the current versioning page says there is no negotiation handshake and that modern MCP carries version and capabilities per request. That is a real disagreement between official pages. Sources: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28 https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/versioning

**Inference**

Putting those pages together, the best reading is: for a **current** stdio server, `initialize` is not part of normal operation; the server’s required behaviors are per-request metadata handling, `server/discover`, JSON-RPC newline framing on stdio, and correct `tools/list` behavior. `initialize` matters only if the server chooses to be dual-era for backward compatibility. This is an inference from the cited current-version pages, not a single sentence stated verbatim in one page. Sources: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/versioning https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports/stdio https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/discover https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/tools

**Uncertainty / Lack Of Good Evidence**

I did not find a current official page that redefines modern `initialize`, because the current revision appears to have removed it rather than changed it. The only concrete `initialize` requirements I found are on the archived legacy `2025-11-25` lifecycle page. Sources: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/versioning https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/lifecycle

I also did not find evidence in the current stdio transport page that `tools/list` gets any stdio-specific exception to the normal per-request `_meta` rules; the evidence points the other way, because the stdio page says request metadata is inline in the JSON-RPC body and there is no header layer. Sources: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports/stdio https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/schema
